claim_records.text: OReX is a method for 3D shape reconstruction from slices alone that uses a Neural Field as the interpolation prior.
A modest neural network in OReX is trained on input planes to return an inside/outside estimate for a given 3D coordinate, yielding a prior that induces smoothness and self-similarities.

fact_fields.method: modest neural network trained on input planes

claim_records.text: The main challenge for the neural field interpolation approach is high-frequency details, as the neural prior is overly smoothing.

OReX offers an iterative estimation architecture and a hierarchical input sampling scheme that encourage coarse-to-fine training, allowing the training process to focus on high frequencies at later stages.

fact_fields.method: iterative estimation architecture and hierarchical input sampling scheme

claim_records.text: A ripple-like effect stemming from the mesh extraction step is identified and analyzed in the OReX approach.
OReX mitigates the ripple-like effect by regularizing the spatial gradients of the indicator function around input in/out boundaries during network training.

fact_fields.method: regularizing spatial gradients of the indicator function around input in/out boundaries during network training

claim_records.text: OReX is demonstrated to be robust, accurate, and scales well with the size of the input through extensive qualitative and quantitative experimentation.
OReX reports state-of-the-art results compared to previous approaches and recent potential solutions.

claims: OReX is a method for 3D shape reconstruction from slices alone that uses a Neural Field as the interpolation prior.
A modest neural network in OReX is trained on input planes to return an inside/outside estimate for a given 3D coordinate, yielding a prior that induces smoothness and self-similarities.
The main challenge for the neural field interpolation approach is high-frequency details, as the neural prior is overly smoothing.

OReX offers an iterative estimation architecture and a hierarchical input sampling scheme that encourage coarse-to-fine training, allowing the training process to focus on high frequencies at later stages.
A ripple-like effect stemming from the mesh extraction step is identified and analyzed in the OReX approach.
OReX mitigates the ripple-like effect by regularizing the spatial gradients of the indicator function around input in/out boundaries during network training.
OReX is demonstrated to be robust, accurate, and scales well with the size of the input through extensive qualitative and quantitative experimentation.
OReX reports state-of-the-art results compared to previous approaches and recent potential solutions.

RayGauss achieves superior rendering quality compared to the state-of-the-art while maintaining reasonable training times.

RayGauss provides a physically consistent formulation of emitted radiance c and density σ decomposed with Gaussian functions associated with Spherical Gaussians/Harmonics for all-frequency colorimetric representation.
RayGauss introduces differentiable ray casting of irregularly distributed Gaussians using an algorithm that integrates radiance fields slab by slab and leverages a BVH structure.
RayGauss's approach finely adapts to the scene while avoiding splatting artifacts.

RayGauss proposes a novel definition of radiance fields based on their decomposition into a weighted sum of locally supported elliptical basis functions with optimizable positions, orientations, and scales.
RayGauss combines spherical harmonics (SH) and spherical Gaussians (SG) with elliptical basis functions to better represent high-frequency color variations such as specular reflections.
Splatting-based methods like 3D Gaussian Splatting cause artifacts when deviating from training views, such as flickering due to a sudden change in primitives ordering.
RayGauss's Volume Raycasting algorithm avoids the artifacts of Splatting, such as flickering.

RayGauss's ray casting algorithm for sparse basis functions sequentially integrates the radiance field slab-by-slab, accumulating colorimetric properties along the ray in slabs of space corresponding to multiple samples.

RayGauss's ray casting algorithm and its backpropagation rely on a Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) implemented on GPU with the OptiX library, enabling interactive rendering times and reasonable training times.

NeRF uses differentiable Volume Ray Casting that computes a discretized version of the volumetric rendering equation using N samples along the ray, assuming fields are piecewise constant in samples neighborhood.

The NeRF MLP FΘ first processes the input 3D coordinate x with 8 fully-connected layers using ReLU activations and 256 channels per layer, outputting σ and a 256-dimensional feature vector.

The 256-dimensional feature vector output by the density-processing layers is concatenated with the camera ray's viewing direction and passed to one additional fully-connected layer using ReLU activation and 128 channels that outputs the view-dependent RGB color.

In hierarchical volume sampling, normalized weights ŵi = wi / sum_{j=1}^{Nc} wj produce a piecewise-constant PDF along the ray, from which a second set of Nf locations is sampled using inverse transform sampling.

NeRF introduces two improvements to enable representing high-resolution complex scenes: positional encoding of input coordinates to assist the MLP in representing high-frequency functions, and a hierarchical sampling procedure for efficient sampling of this high-frequency representation.
In NeRF experiments, the positional encoding parameter L is set to 10 for the 3D coordinate x and L = 4 for the Cartesian viewing direction unit vector d.

claim_records.text: MobileNeRF represents a NeRF as a set of textured polygons where textures represent binary opacities and feature vectors, enabling rendering with standard polygon rasterization pipelines.

MobileNeRF renders images by z-buffering textured polygons to produce a feature vector at every pixel, which is interpreted by a small view-dependent MLP running in a fragment shader to produce final pixel color.

fact_fields.method: Polygon rasterization with fragment shader MLP for final color

claim_records.text: MobileNeRF achieves interactive frame rates on a wide range of compute platforms including mobile phones by utilizing the traditional polygon rasterization pipeline's massive pixel-level parallelism.

Traditional NeRF implementations evaluate a large MLP at hundreds of sample positions along the ray for each pixel to estimate and integrate density and radiance, making the rendering process far too slow for interactive visualization.

SNeRG's precomputation and deferred rendering approach increases NeRF rendering speed by three orders of magnitude, but still relies on ray marching through a sparse voxel grid and requires significant GPU memory.
MobileNeRF is 10× faster than SNeRG with the same output quality on standard test scenes.

fact_fields.method: MobileNeRF vs SNeRG rendering speed comparison

claim_records.text: MobileNeRF's rendering pipeline does not sample rays or sort polygons in depth order, and thus can model only binary opacities.
MobileNeRF consumes less memory than SNeRG by storing surface textures instead of volumetric textures, enabling it to run on integrated GPUs with limited memory and power.

fact_fields.method: Surface texture storage vs volumetric texture storage

claim_records.text: MobileNeRF allows real-time manipulation of reconstructed objects/scenes because they are represented as simple triangle meshes.
MobileNeRF does not need reconstructed 3D geometry as input, unlike many prior real-time view synthesis methods.
Rendering a standard NeRF involves evaluating a large neural network at multiple 3D locations per pixel, preventing real-time rendering.
MobileNeRF caches outgoing radiance, which does not need expensive compute to model global illumination effects and results in higher view-synthesis quality compared to methods like NVDiffRec.

claim_records.text: Progressive Volume Distillation (PVD) is a systematic distillation method that enables any-to-any conversions between different NeRF architectures, including MLP, sparse or low-rank tensors, hashtables and their compositions.
PVD performs distillation progressively on different levels of volume representations, from shallower to deeper, to enable fast architecture conversions.
PVD employs special treatment of density to address its specific numerical instability problem during distillation.
Empirical validation of PVD is conducted on the NeRF-Synthetic, LLFF and TanksAndTemples datasets.

Using PVD, an MLP-based NeRF model distilled from a hashtable-based Instant-NGP model achieves a 10×~20× faster speed than training the original NeRF from scratch, while achieving a superior level of synthesis quality.
Hashtable-based NeRF representations admit faster training and rendering but their lack of clear geometric meaning hampers downstream tasks like spatial-relation-aware editing.

A NeRF model distilled by PVD from an INGP teacher within 1.5 hours achieves improved synthesis quality and reduced training time compared to a NeRF trained from scratch using 25 hours on the Family and Barn scene from the TanksAndTemples dataset.
TensoRF leverages VM (vector-matrix) decomposition and canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) to produce compact feature tensor representations for NeRF.
Instant Neural Graphics Primitives (INGP) utilizes multilevel hash tables for effective compression of feature tensors in NeRF.

NeRF methods with explicit or hybrid representation usually enjoy faster training due to shallower representations and cope better with geometric-aware editing such as merging and other scene manipulations, compared to purely implicit representations.

PVD builds a block-wise distillation strategy to accelerate training based on a unified view of different NeRF architectures, and employs special treatment of the dynamic density volume range by clipping to improve training stability and synthesis quality.
Distillation from hashtable and VM-decomposition structures often helps boost student model synthesis quality and consumes less time than training from scratch.

claim_records.text: NeRF generates a volumetric representation called a radiance field that creates color and density for every point within the relevant 3D space, rather than directly restoring the whole 3D scene geometry.

CAMPARI simultaneously learns a camera generator and an image generator, enabling use of complex camera distributions without manual tuning, and represents scenes through foreground and background decomposition to achieve 3D-consistent representations and accurate camera distribution recovery.
CAMPARI surpasses baseline models that heavily depend on accurately matched camera distributions, due to its performance without camera parameter tuning.
CAMPARI faces the challenge of generating inward-facing faces compared to the traditional inverted faces (hollow face illusion) where convex faces appear concave.
Pix2NeRF introduces a pipeline to generate NeRF from a single input image, built upon π-GAN which maps latent codes to radiance fields.
Pix2NeRF employs an unsupervised approach and can be trained with independent images, offering potential applications in 3D avatar generation, novel view synthesis, and super-resolution.
Pix2NeRF is currently restricted to work with only one category per dataset, impeding its ability to generalize to new categories.
Pix2NeRF is built on top of π-GAN but is not limited to using π-GAN as its backbone; newer generative NeRF models such as EG3D may achieve better visual quality if used as a backbone.

NeRF uses a deep neural network to represent complex scenes in a fully connected, non-convolutional way, with input as a continuous 5D coordinate and output as volume density and view-dependent emitted radiance at that spatial location.
NeRF uses classic volume rendering techniques to synthesize views and is optimized using a set of images with known camera poses.

NeRF introduces positional encoding and a hierarchical sampling strategy to address the inefficiency of the basic implementation, and can represent non-Lambertian effects such as specularities using input viewing direction.
NeRF uses a separate neural continuous volume representation network for each scene.

claim_records.text: Hyb-NeRF is a novel neural radiance field with a multi-resolution hybrid encoding that achieves efficient neural modeling and fast rendering while enabling high-quality novel view synthesis, using memory-efficient learnable positional features at coarse resolutions and fast-optimizing hash-based feature grids at fine resolutions.
Cone tracing-based features are embedded in the learnable positional encoding to eliminate encoding ambiguity and reduce aliasing artifacts.

fact_fields.method: cone tracing-based feature embedding in learnable positional encoding

claim_records.text: Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets show that Hyb-NeRF achieves faster rendering speed with better rendering quality and even a lower memory footprint in comparison to previous state-of-the-art methods.

NeRF requires hundreds of network evaluations per pixel to approximate a volume rendering integral, making it slow to train, while caching NeRFs into explicit data structures enhances rendering speed at the cost of higher memory usage.
On the ficus scene in Blender, Hyb-NeRF with 16.4M parameters achieves 35.85 PSNR and 0.986 SSIM, outperforming JNGP with 24.4M parameters which achieves 33.23 PSNR and 0.981 SSIM.
Hyb-NeRF can render high-quality color images and synthesize an alpha map with less noise, enabling accurate reconstruction of the translucency of leaf edges without jaggies on the ficus scene.
In comparison with previous state-of-the-art fast NeRF training methods, Hyb-NeRF models achieve the best rendering quality and memory compactness while maintaining fast rendering.

fact_fields.method: Hyb-NeRF vs fast NeRF training methods comparison

claim_records.text: NeRF and its variants encode the input 5D coordinate as a multi-resolution sequence of Fourier features using fixed positional encodings, requiring a large MLP to transform non-parametric features into color and density, leading to lengthy training and rendering times.

Caching neural radiance fields into explicit data structures allows learning color and density with a much shallower MLP, improving rendering speed at the cost of storing a large set of features in a discrete data structure.

fact_fields.method: explicit data structure caching for NeRF

claim_records.text: Instant NGP employs multi-resolution voxel grids of trainable features with multi-resolution hash encoding to map grids to fixed-size feature arrays from coarse to fine resolution, reducing MLP computational burden and significantly increasing training speed.

Hash-based multi-resolution grid representation has limited representation power and low memory efficiency at coarse resolution levels, as trainable features at coarse levels have lower resolutions and are less compressed than fine-level feature grids.

Hyb-NeRF uses coarse-to-fine hybrid features to model scene geometry details and colors, replacing coarse-level parametric feature grids with a learnable positional encoding with far fewer trainable parameters, then concatenating learnable positional features with fine-level multi-resolution feature grids for multi-resolution scene representation.
The learnable positional encoding in Hyb-NeRF adaptively learns the weights of positional features to improve memory efficiency and rendering quality.
Embedding cone tracing-based positional features in the learning of positional feature weights helps disambiguate the optimization process and eliminate aliasing artifacts.
All Hyb-NeRF models can reconstruct high-quality radiance fields in 9 minutes.

The smallest Hyb-NeRF model with 8.4M trainable parameters takes 4 minutes to achieve better rendering quality than state-of-the-art methods while requiring substantially less memory than previous and concurrent voxel-based methods.

claim_records.text: Fourier PlenOctrees suffer from artifacts introduced by the involved compression when combined with recent state-of-the-art techniques for training static per-frame NeRF models.

The proposed FPO++ density encoding adapts Fourier-based compression to the characteristics of the transfer function used by the underlying volume rendering procedure, leading to a substantial reduction of artifacts in the dynamic model.
FPO++ includes an augmentation of the training data that relaxes the periodicity assumption of the Fourier compression.
PlenOctrees use a hierarchical octree structure of density and view-dependent radiance in terms of spherical harmonics to entirely avoid network evaluations during rendering.
Instant-NGP incorporated a multi-resolution hash encoding to significantly accelerate the training of neural models including NeRF.
Plenoxels stored spherical harmonics and opacity values within a sparse voxel grid.
TensoRF factorized dense voxel grids into multiple low-rank components.
NeRF synthesizes novel views using volume rendering of density and view-dependent radiance optimized in an implicit neural scene representation using MLPs from posed images.
Fourier PlenOctrees (FPO) extended ordinary PlenOctrees by combining them with the Fourier transform to enable handling time-variant density and SH-based radiance in an efficient way.
During FPO construction, compression is performed on encoded densities σ′ = ecomp(elog(σ)), where the encoding consists of a component-dependent and a logarithmic part.
The proposed component-dependent and logarithmic density encoding allows for better reconstruction of original densities without fine-tuning than can be achieved with only DFT and IDFT.
The logarithmic density encoding is defined as elog(σ) = log(σ + 1), applied to non-negative density values before DFT.
The logarithmic density encoding focuses approximation on densities near or equal to zero by mapping larger density values closer together while keeping smaller values almost unchanged.
The L2-error in fine-tuning is allowed to be larger for encoded high density values than without logarithmic encoding, focusing optimization on more important parts of the reconstruction.

The logarithmic density encoding is defined as elog(σ) = log(σ + 1), applied to non-negative density values before DFT.
The logarithmic density encoding focuses approximation on densities near or equal to zero by mapping larger density values closer together while keeping smaller values almost unchanged.
The L2-error in fine-tuning is allowed to be larger for encoded high density values than without logarithmic encoding, focusing optimization on more important parts of the reconstruction.

claim_records.text: NerfDiff distills knowledge of a 3D-aware conditional diffusion model (CDM) into NeRF through synthesizing and refining a set of virtual views at test time.
NerfDiff significantly outperforms existing NeRF-based and geometry-free approaches on the ShapeNet, ABO, and Clevr3D datasets.
NerfDiff can predict sharp renderings despite large occlusion, whereas VisionNeRF cannot handle this uncertainty and shows implausible blurring.
Standard NeRF requires tens or hundreds of images for overfitting a scene and has no generalization ability to infer new scenes.
Generalizable NeRF models conditioned by projection of 3D points and gathering of corresponding image features produce blurry results when target views are far from the input.
2D generative model-based approaches for single-image view synthesis are only able to synthesize partially 3D-consistent images.

fact_fields.method: 2D generative model-based single-image view synthesis approaches

claim_records.text: At training stage, NerfDiff jointly trains a camera-space triplane-based NeRF together with a 3D-aware conditional diffusion model on a collection of scenes.
A naive finetuning strategy of optimizing NeRF parameters directly using CDM outputs leads to subpar renderings because CDM outputs tend to be multi-view inconsistent.

fact_fields.method: Naive NeRF finetuning using CDM outputs

claim_records.text: NerfDiff's NeRF-guided distillation updates the NeRF representation and guides the multi-view diffusion process in an alternating fashion.
NerfDiff introduces an efficient image-conditioned NeRF representation based on camera-aligned triplanes.
NerfDiff's 3D-aware conditional diffusion model integrates volume rendering into 2D diffusion models to facilitate generalization to novel views.
Direct 3D-space diffusion methods for 3D generation require 3D ground truth for learning the diffusion process, which is hard to acquire in the real environment.
Early single-view 3D reconstruction methods relied on ground truth training data to estimate geometry by mapping images to depth or directly to 3D shapes.
Differentiable renderer-based 3D reconstruction methods that provide estimates without ground truth 3D supervision were limited to reconstructing only geometry, not appearance.

claim_records.text: EvaSurf uses an efficient surface-based model paired with a multi-view supervision module to ensure accurate mesh reconstruction.
EvaSurf learns an implicit texture embedded with a set of Gaussian lobes to capture view-dependent information for high-fidelity rendering.
EvaSurf employs a lightweight neural shader alongside explicit geometry and implicit texture to reduce computation cost and support real-time rendering on common mobile devices.
EvaSurf can reconstruct high-quality appearance and accurate mesh on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
EvaSurf can be trained in 1-2 hours using a single GPU.
EvaSurf runs on mobile devices at over 40 FPS.
The final rendering package required for EvaSurf takes up only 40-50 MB.

claim_records.text: NeRF achieves impressive view synthesis results for 360 capture of bounded scenes and forward-facing capture of bounded and unbounded scenes.

NeRF's success in avoiding shape-radiance ambiguity is analyzed in the technical report.
The proposed method improves view synthesis fidelity for 360 captures of objects within large-scale, unbounded 3D scenes.
Code for the method is available at https://github.com/Kai-46/nerfplusplus.

claim_records.text: Standard NeRF yields blurred rendering results when training images are captured at non-uniform scales.
Standard NeRF produces aliasing artifacts when test images are taken from distant views.

Mip-NeRF uses a conical frustum multiscale representation to encode scale information, but is only suitable for offline rendering because it relies on integrated positional encoding (IPE) to query a multilayer perceptron (MLP).

Mip-VoG is an explicit multiscale representation with a deferred architecture designed for real-time anti-aliasing rendering, consisting of a density Mip-VoG for scene geometry and a feature Mip-VoG paired with a small MLP for view-dependent color.

Mip-VoG encodes scene scale using the level of detail (LOD) derived from ray differentials, and uses quadrilinear interpolation to map a queried 3D location to its features and density from two neighboring downsampled voxel grids.
Mip-VoG is the first approach to simultaneously offer multiscale training and real-time anti-aliasing rendering.
Experiments on multiscale datasets show Mip-VoG outperforms state-of-the-art real-time rendering baselines.

claim_records.text: Spatial grid-accelerated NeRFs do not explicitly reason about scale, and introduce aliasing artifacts when reconstructing scenes captured at different camera distances.
Mip-NeRF and its extensions use scale-aware renderers that project volumetric frustums rather than point samples, but rely on positional encodings that are not readily compatible with grid methods.
PyNeRF modifies grid-based NeRF models by training model heads at different spatial grid resolutions, and uses coarser grids to render samples that cover larger volumes at render time.
PyNeRF can be easily applied to existing accelerated NeRF methods, and reduces error rates by 20-90% across synthetic and unbounded real-world scenes while incurring minimal performance overhead.
Compared to Mip-NeRF, PyNeRF reduces error rates by 20% while training over 60x faster.

claims: The proposed differentiable rendering framework formulates the lighting of a static scene as one neural incident light field (NeILF) and one outgoing neural radiance field (NeRF) for joint geometry, material, and lighting estimation from multi-view images.

The union of incident and outgoing light fields via physically-based rendering and inter-reflections between surfaces enables disentanglement of scene geometry, material, and lighting from image observations in a physically-based manner.
The proposed incident light and inter-reflection framework can be applied to other NeRF systems, and can decompose outgoing radiance into incident lights and surface materials.
The proposed incident light and inter-reflection framework acts as a surface refinement module that further improves the reconstruction detail of the neural surface.
The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results in geometry reconstruction quality, material estimation accuracy, and fidelity of novel view rendering on several datasets.

claim_records.text: NeRF's performance for novel view synthesis drops significantly when the number of available input views is reduced.
The majority of artifacts in sparse input NeRF scenarios are caused by errors in estimated scene geometry and divergent behavior at the start of training.
RegNeRF regularizes geometry and appearance of patches rendered from unobserved viewpoints, and anneals the ray sampling space during training to address sparse-input NeRF artifacts.
RegNeRF additionally uses a normalizing flow model to regularize the color of unobserved viewpoints.

RegNeRF outperforms other single-scene optimization methods, and in many cases also outperforms conditional models extensively pre-trained on large multi-view datasets, for sparse-input view synthesis.

claim_records.text: NeRF and its variants require lengthy training time ranging from hours to days to reconstruct a single scene.
The presented direct voxel grid optimization approach achieves NeRF-comparable quality and converges from scratch in less than 15 minutes with a single GPU.
The direct voxel grid optimization method uses a density voxel grid for scene geometry and a feature voxel grid with a shallow network for complex view-dependent appearance.
Post-activation interpolation on voxel density is capable of producing sharp surfaces in lower grid resolution.
Direct voxel density optimization is prone to suboptimal geometry solutions, so the method imposes several priors to robustify the optimization process.

Evaluation on five inward-facing benchmarks shows the direct voxel grid optimization method matches, if not surpasses, NeRF's quality, while taking about 15 minutes to train from scratch for a new scene.

claim_records.text: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) has low rendering efficiency because rendering a single pixel requires multiple network forwardings.

Existing NeRF acceleration methods either reduce the number of required samples or optimize network forwarding implementation, but the multiple sampling problem persists due to the intrinsic representation of radiance fields.

Neural Light Fields (NeLF) reduce NeRF computation cost by requiring only one network forwarding per pixel, but existing NeLF methods need significantly larger network capacities to achieve visual quality close to NeRF, limiting practical rendering efficiency.

The proposed Neural Radiance Distribution Field (NeRDF) uses a small network similar to NeRF while preserving NeLF-style single network forwarding per pixel rendering speed, by modeling radiance distribution along each ray with frequency basis and predicting frequency weights via the network, then computing pixel values via volume rendering on radiance distributions.

NeRDF achieves approximately 254x speed-up over NeRF with similar network size, with only a marginal performance decline, delivering a better trade-off among speed, quality, and network size than existing methods.

claim_records.text: Current implicit neural representation methods for surface reconstruction and novel view synthesis have inherent computational complexity that constrains attainable frame rates and resolutions in practical applications.

The proposed VQ-NeRF pipeline reduces NeRF sampling space to a lower resolution and restores it to original size using a pre-trained VAE decoder to mitigate the sampling time bottleneck during rendering.

High compression rates make reconstructing fine scene texture details challenging even when the codebook provides representative features, so VQ-NeRF uses a multi-scale NeRF sampling scheme that concurrently optimizes the NeRF model at both compressed and original scales to enhance fine detail preservation.
VQ-NeRF incorporates a semantic loss function to improve geometric fidelity and semantic coherence of 3D reconstructions.
VQ-NeRF achieves the optimal trade-off between rendering quality and efficiency, with superior performance confirmed via evaluation on the DTU, BlendMVS, and H3DS datasets.

claim_records.text: Meshes, voxels, point clouds, and NeRF-based neural implicit fields are task-specific 3D representations lacking universal applicability across reconstruction, generation, editing, and driving.
Meshes offer high precision but their dense vertex data complicates editing.
NeRFs deliver excellent rendering but suffer from structural ambiguity, hindering animation and manipulation.
All existing 3D representations inherently struggle with the trade-off between data complexity and fidelity.

The novel 3D Hierarchical Proxy Node representation represents an object's shape and texture via a sparse set of hierarchically organized (tree-structured) proxy nodes distributed on its surface and interior.
Each proxy node stores local shape and texture information implicitly encoded by a small MLP within its neighborhood.
Querying any 3D coordinate's properties involves efficient neural interpolation and lightweight decoding from relevant nearby and parent nodes.
The Hierarchical Proxy Node framework yields a highly compact representation where nodes align with local semantics, enabling direct drag-and-edit manipulation.
The Hierarchical Proxy Node framework offers scalable quality-complexity control.
Extensive experiments across 3D reconstruction and editing demonstrate the method's expressive efficiency, high-fidelity rendering quality, and superior editability.

claim_records.text: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) typically struggle to reconstruct and render highly specular objects, whose appearance varies quickly with changes in viewpoint.
Recent works have improved NeRF's ability to render detailed specular appearance of distant environment illumination, but are unable to synthesize consistent reflections of closer content.
Recent NeRF specular rendering techniques rely on large computationally-expensive neural networks to model outgoing radiance, which severely limits optimization and rendering speed.

The proposed NeRF-Casting approach casts reflection rays from points along each camera ray and traces them through the NeRF representation to render feature vectors which are decoded into color using a small inexpensive network, instead of querying an expensive neural network for outgoing view-dependent radiance.
The NeRF-Casting model outperforms prior methods for view synthesis of scenes containing shiny objects.
NeRF-Casting is the only existing NeRF method that can synthesize photorealistic specular appearance and reflections in real-world scenes.
NeRF-Casting requires comparable optimization time to current state-of-the-art view synthesis models.

claim_records.text: RT-NeRF is described as the first algorithm-hardware co-design acceleration of NeRF.

RT-NeRF leverages a coarse-grained view-dependent computing ordering scheme to eliminate unnecessary processing of invisible points.

claim_records.text: Standard NeRF uses straight rays and fails to handle complicated light path changes caused by refraction and reflection, preventing successful synthesis of transparent or specular objects.
NeRRF takes object silhouette as input and uses marching tetrahedra with progressive encoding to reconstruct the geometry of non-Lambertian objects.
NeRRF models refraction and reflection effects of non-Lambertian objects in a unified framework using Fresnel terms.
NeRRF proposes a virtual cone supersampling technique to achieve efficient and effective anti-aliasing.
NeRRF is benchmarked on different shapes, backgrounds and Fresnel terms on both real-world and synthetic datasets.

NeRRF supports editing applications including material editing, object replacement/insertion, and environment illumination estimation, with qualitatively and quantitatively benchmarked rendering results.

fact_fields.method: qualitative and quantitative benchmarking of NeRRF editing applications

claim_records.text: NeRRF codes and data are publicly available at https://github.com/dawning77/NeRRF.

claim_records.text: 3DGS is introduced into indoor 3D Object Detection for the first time in this work.

fact_fields.method: Introducing 3D Gaussian Splatting into indoor 3D Object Detection

claim_records.text: 3DGS primarily relies on 2D pixel-level supervision, resulting in unclear 3D spatial distribution of Gaussian blobs and poor differentiation between objects and background, which hinders indoor 3DOD.
2D images typically include numerous background pixels, leading to densely reconstructed 3DGS with many noisy Gaussian blobs representing the background, negatively affecting detection.
Incorporating 2D Boundary Guidance significantly enhances the spatial distribution of Gaussian blobs, resulting in clearer differentiation between objects and their background.

The proposed Box-Focused Sampling strategy uses 2D boxes to generate object probability distribution in 3D space, enabling effective probabilistic sampling in 3D to retain more object blobs and reduce noisy background blobs.
3DGS-DET achieves an improvement of +6.0 on mAP@0.25 over NeRF-Det++ on the ScanNet dataset.

claim_records.text: VDN-NeRF is a method to train neural radiance fields for improved geometry under non-Lambertian surface and dynamic lighting conditions that cause significant variation in the radiance of a point when viewed from different angles.
VDN-NeRF normalizes view-dependence by distilling invariant information already encoded in learned NeRFs, rather than explicitly modeling underlying factors that produce view-dependent phenomena.
VDN-NeRF jointly trains NeRFs for view synthesis with view-dependence normalization to attain quality geometry.

Experiments show that the proposed view-dependence normalization can minimize the effect of shape-radiance ambiguity on geometry, aligning the optimal capacity needed for explaining view-dependent variations.
VDN-NeRF applies to various baselines and significantly improves geometry without changing the volume rendering pipeline, even if data is captured under a moving light source.

claim_records.text: Neural approaches such as NeRF have achieved remarkable success in view synthesis but do not explicitly perform decomposition and instead operate exclusively on radiance, the product of reflectance and illumination.
Extensions to NeRF such as NeRD can perform decomposition but struggle to accurately recover detailed illumination, thereby significantly limiting realism.
The proposed reflectance decomposition network can estimate shape, BRDF, and per-image illumination given a set of object images captured under varying illumination.
Neural-PIL is an illumination integration network that replaces a costly illumination integral operation in the rendering with a simple network query.
Novel smooth manifold auto-encoders are used to learn deep low-dimensional priors on BRDF and illumination representations.
The proposed decompositions result in considerably better BRDF and light estimates, enabling more accurate novel view-synthesis and relighting compared to prior art.

claim_records.text: Previous works such as IDR and NeuS overlook the spatial context in 3D space when predicting and rendering the surface, thereby may fail to capture sharp local topologies such as small holes and structures.
NeuDA is a flexible neural implicit representation leveraging hierarchical voxel grids for high-fidelity surface reconstruction.
NeuDA maintains hierarchical anchor grids where each vertex stores a 3D position (or anchor) instead of the direct embedding (or feature).
NeuDA optimizes the anchor grids such that different local geometry structures can be adaptively encoded.
NeuDA introduces a simple hierarchical positional encoding method for the hierarchical anchor structure to flexibly exploit the properties of high-frequency and low-frequency geometry and appearance.
Experiments on both the DTU and BlendedMVS datasets demonstrate that NeuDA can produce promising mesh surfaces.

claim_records.text: HollowNeRF is a compression solution for hashgrid-based NeRF that automatically sparsifies the feature grid during the training phase.

HollowNeRF trains a coarse 3D saliency mask to guide efficient feature pruning, and employs an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) pruner to sparsify the 3D saliency mask during training.
HollowNeRF delivers comparable rendering quality to Instant-NGP while utilizing just 31% of the parameters.
HollowNeRF can achieve a PSNR accuracy gain of up to 1dB using only 56% of the parameters.

claim_records.text: OReX is a method for 3D shape reconstruction from slices alone that uses a Neural Field as the interpolation prior.
A modest neural network in OReX is trained on input planes to return an inside/outside estimate for a given 3D coordinate, yielding a prior that induces smoothness and self-similarities.

fact_fields.method: modest neural network trained on input planes

claim_records.text: The main challenge for the neural field interpolation approach is high-frequency details, as the neural prior is overly smoothing.

OReX offers an iterative estimation architecture and a hierarchical input sampling scheme that encourage coarse-to-fine training, allowing the training process to focus on high frequencies at later stages.

fact_fields.method: iterative estimation architecture and hierarchical input sampling scheme

claim_records.text: A ripple-like effect stemming from the mesh extraction step is identified and analyzed in the OReX approach.
OReX mitigates the ripple-like effect by regularizing the spatial gradients of the indicator function around input in/out boundaries during network training.

fact_fields.method: regularizing spatial gradients of the indicator function around input in/out boundaries during network training

claim_records.text: OReX is demonstrated to be robust, accurate, and scales well with the size of the input through extensive qualitative and quantitative experimentation.
OReX reports state-of-the-art results compared to previous approaches and recent potential solutions.
The benefit of OReX's individual contributions is demonstrated through analysis and ablation studies.

Previous works addressing 3D shape reconstruction from sparse planar cross-sections either produce low quality results, or rely on additional priors such as target topology, appearance information, or input normal directions.

The input for 3D shape reconstruction from planar cross-sections is an in/out indicator function fully defined on a sparse collection of planes in space, and the output is an interpolation of the indicator function to the entire volume.
